audit.whatIsWrong: Four strings put the damage reflect on Mel's ultimate: spikes[2] 'before she can angle her R damage-reflect', wants.you[1] 'she can't pre-position her R reflect', wants.foe[1] 'Hold R to reflect your committed R/AA burst', mid 'angle her R damage-reflect... when she's holding R'. The reflect is Rebuttal (W). Riot on R Golden Eclipse: 'Mel strikes all enemies marked with Overwhelm regardless of their distance from her' — no reflect at all.
audit.why: The reader is told to fear the wrong button on the wrong cooldown. Golden Eclipse is 120/100/80 and global; Rebuttal is 38s at rank 1 falling to 26s and only 250 range. Playing around a 120s ult when the real gate is a 38s barrier means either never committing, or committing into a Rebuttal that is up every single time.
audit.corrected: Rebuttal (W) is the reflect, 38s at rank 1; Golden Eclipse is a global Overwhelm strike with no reflect.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rebuttal reflects projectiles and Seismic Shard is a projectile. No string warns against opening with Q into a Mel holding W.
audit.why: This is the same interaction the mirror audit (audits/top/mel__malphite.json) identified from her side, where the page had told her NOT to use Rebuttal on his Q. Stated from this side it is a hard rule: your only ranged tool comes straight back at you if you throw it into her barrier, and Rebuttal also prevents her taking damage for the duration, so the cast is wasted twice over.
audit.corrected: Never open with Seismic Shard into a held Rebuttal — it is a projectile and it returns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Her poke is called 'ranged Q overload' in five places. It is Radiant Volley, 950 range, 10s at rank 1 down to 6s. late also claims she has 'no untargetability to dodge my R' while Rebuttal 'prevents her from taking damage'.
audit.why: Packet defect: 'never names any of Mel's abilities'. Beyond the name, the 950-versus-625 range gap and the 10s cadence are what make 'do not walk up' concrete. And she does have a damage-immunity window — it is not untargetability, but functionally it answers a committed R, which is the opposite of what the late paragraph promises.
audit.corrected: Radiant Volley (950 range, 10s at rank 1); Rebuttal prevents her taking damage for its duration.

audit.whatIsWrong: Golden Eclipse's global range is never stated — it is 25000, striking every enemy carrying Overwhelm regardless of distance.
audit.why: The late paragraph's plan is to disengage and let armour wall her out. Distance is not a defence against a global execute payout, so the actual answer is to not have Overwhelm stacked on you when it comes up, not to walk away from her.
audit.corrected: Golden Eclipse reaches you at any range once Overwhelm is stacked.
sources: champ-data/_kits/mel.json (R Golden Eclipse, range 25000, P Searing Brilliance Overwhelm)

audit.whatIsWrong: content.win[3] gives Malphite Levels 4-5. The mirror audit for Mel proposes the same stage move from 'Malphite' to 'Skill' on her page, on the grounds that Unstoppable Force does not exist yet at 4-5 and she out-ranges him with her whole kit.
audit.why: The two directions must not disagree, and the mirror's reasoning holds from this side too: at 4-5 Malphite has no gap-closer, Radiant Volley reaches 950 to Seismic Shard's 625, and the only thing that changed is that Thunderclap now feeds Ground Slam. Stabilising is not winning.
audit.corrected: win[3] Malphite to Skill, matching the mirror, with whys[3] restated to match.
sources: audits/top/mel__malphite.json (edit: content win[3] Malphite to Skill)
champ-data/_kits/malphite.json (R Unstoppable Force is the level-6 spike)

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike is described as flanking 'before she can angle her R damage-reflect' — right timing, wrong ability, wrong cooldown.
audit.why: The spike is real and it is the whole matchup. Attaching it to Rebuttal's 38s rather than an imagined ult reflect tells the reader what they are actually waiting for.
audit.corrected: Level-6 spike restated against Rebuttal's 38s barrier.

edits.after: Radiant Volley still out-ranges me 950 to 625 and armor does nothing to magic — but Thunderclap feeds Ground Slam, so I farm level.

edits.after: Land Unstoppable Force from fog so Rebuttal (W, 38s) is not facing me — it reflects projectiles

edits.after: Poke with Radiant Volley (Q, 950 range, 10s at rank 1) every time you step up for a CS

edits.after: Hold Rebuttal (W) for Seismic Shard — it is a projectile and it comes straight back at you

edits.after: Unstoppable Force flips the lane — I flank from fog and knock up a squishy mage with no escape while Rebuttal faces the wrong way.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are where I stop bleeding: Thunderclap gives me bonus armor and empowers my autos, Ground Slam clears the wave and slows her attack speed if she ever steps up, and Granite Shield refreshes between her Q casts so I farm through the poke. Level 6 is the entire lane — Unstoppable Force lets me flank from fog and knock her up before she can angle her R damage-reflect, and a squishy ranged mage with no escape dies to one R-in collapse. Do NOT ult straight into her face when she's holding R; come from the side or the brush so the reflect and her W/E never line up.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are where I stop bleeding: Thunderclap gives me bonus armor that Ground Slam then turns into damage, and Granite Shield refreshes between her Radiant Volley casts so I farm through the poke. Level 6 is the entire lane — Unstoppable Force lets me flank from fog and knock her up, and a squishy ranged mage with no escape dies to one R-in collapse. Get the button right, though: Rebuttal (W) is the reflect, not her ult, and at 38s it is up far more often than a 120s Golden Eclipse. It returns projectiles, so never open with Seismic Shard into a Mel holding W.

edits.before: This is the rare scaling lane the tank wins: Mel is a squishy artillery mage with no percent-HP or true damage and no untargetability to dodge my R, so my armor stacking just walls her out. Once I hit first item I out-durable her poke entirely and every R-in is a free pick or fight-opener on a 5-second-to-die carry. Her only path back is to play fully safe behind her team and chunk me with Q before I reach her — so I never go in head-on into a held R, I flank, and I use her as the kill target every teamfight.
edits.after: This is the rare scaling lane the tank wins: Mel has no percent-HP and no true damage, so health stacking walls her out — armor does nothing to magic, but it does feed Ground Slam. Once I hit first item every R-in is a free pick on a 5-second-to-die carry. Two things still answer me. Rebuttal prevents her taking damage while it holds, so I flank onto a spent W, never a fresh one. And Golden Eclipse reaches me at any distance once Overwhelm is stacked, so backing off is not a defence — dropping the stacks is.

notes: Mirror-checked against audits/top/mel__malphite.json and kept consistent: win[3] moved to Skill on both sides, and the Rebuttal-reflects-Seismic-Shard interaction is now stated from both directions. The reflect was attributed to Mel's ultimate in four separate strings on this page; it is Rebuttal (W), 38s at rank 1 versus Golden Eclipse's 120s, which changes the entire commit schedule. Also corrected: 'no untargetability to dodge my R' — Rebuttal prevents her taking damage for its duration, which functionally answers a committed engage. Added: Golden Eclipse is global (range 25000) and pays out on stacked Overwhelm, so distance is not a defence. Not asserted: whether Unstoppable Force, which the kit file also flags projectile, is itself returnable by Rebuttal — the mirror agent deliberately left that out as unverified and I have matched that decision rather than introduce a disagreement.
